articles.title: Apex Footwear earns just Tk1cr from Tk890cr exports in FY26
articles.desc: Craftsman Footwear and Accessories Limited also reported a 5.83% export margin in FY25, earning Tk4.32 crore against revenue of Tk74 crore.
articles.content: Apex Footwear earns just Tk1cr from Tk890cr exports in FY26 | The Business Standard Apex Footwear earns just Tk1cr from Tk890cr exports in FY26 Last modified: 07 November, 2026, 09:55 pm Apex Footwear to raise Tk500cr thru preference shares to cut debt Envoy Textile, Apex Footwear set board meetings to decide FY26 dividend Apex Footwear's Tk616cr revenue yields just Tk1cr profit amid rising costs, tax pressures Venturini debuts with nobel’s return to fashion spotlight Businesses need relief from ‘tax terrorism’: Apex Footwear MD Nasim Manzur Craftsman Footwear and Accessories Limited also reported a 5.83% export margin in FY25, earning Tk4.32 crore against revenue of Tk74 crore. Last modified: 07 November, 2026, 09:55 pm Despite a 34% surge in export earnings in FY26, Apex Footwear Limited, the country's leading shoe maker, made just Tk1.41 crore in profit from exports, translating into a wafer-thin margin of around 0.16%, according to its audited financial statements. Export revenue rose to Tk890 crore in the financial year ended June 2026, from Tk663 crore in FY25. But higher production costs, financing expenses and tax liabilities largely offset the sales growth. The contrast with smaller competitors is stark. MK Footwear PLC, listed on the Dhaka Stock Exchange's SME platform, earned Tk5.61 crore in profit against Tk90 crore in export revenue in FY26, achieving a margin of 6.29%. In FY25, it earned Tk8.76 crore from exports of Tk79 crore. Keep updated, follow The Business Standard's Google news channel Craftsman Footwear and Accessories Limited also reported a 5.83% export margin in FY25, earning Tk4.32 crore against revenue of Tk74 crore. Apex's export profitability has remained modest over the years. It earned Tk3.17 crore from exports of Tk508 crore in FY21 and Tk5.87 crore on Tk714 crore in FY23. Exports fell to Tk482 crore in FY24 before recovering to Tk663 crore in FY25, when profit plunged to Tk0.37 crore. It recovered to Tk1.41 crore in FY26. The company's cost of goods sold rose 39% to Tk791 crore in FY26, while finance costs increased 49% to Tk58.90 crore. Although it cut export-related marketing and selling expenses by 44%, higher production and borrowing costs continued to squeeze margins. Taxation added to the pressure. An analyst at an asset management company said Apex earned Tk10.79 crore in pre-tax profit from exports but incurred Tk12.65 crore in tax expenses. A Tk3.27 crore deferred tax adjustment income helped offset the shortfall, leaving a net export profit of Tk1.41 crore. The analyst said the figures point to inadequate returns from the company's export business despite substantial sales growth. A senior company official attributed the thin margin largely to tax deducted at source (TDS) on export proceeds. Banks deduct the tax before depositing export earnings into exporters' accounts, but the amount withheld does not necessarily match their actual tax liability for the accounting period. The analyst said footwear exporters pay TDS equivalent to 1% of export value. Although it can be adjusted against final income tax liability, the deduction is non-refundable. Exporters therefore cannot recover any excess if their final tax liability is lower, further squeezing margins. Apex's domestic operations performed better, with local revenue rising 10% to Tk1,218 crore and profit increasing 7% to Tk14.11 crore in FY26. Overall, the company's revenue grew 19% to Tk2,108 crore, crossing Tk2,000 crore for the first time, while total profit rose 15% to Tk15.53 crore. To ease its financing burden, the board has decided to raise up to Tk500 crore through redeemable preference shares to refinance existing loans, subject to shareholder and Bangladesh Securities and Exchange Commission approval. At the end of FY26, Apex had Tk310 crore in long-term loans, Tk260 crore in lease liabilities and Tk2,078 crore in short-term loans. articles.title: AsoBeast 1.16: open-source ASO that finds the keywords your app already ranks for
articles.desc: AsoBeast is an open-source App Store Optimization (ASO) tool and keyword rank tracker for the Apple App Store and Google Play. You can self-host it with Docker or use the hosted version at asobeast.com. Version 1.16 finds the keywords your app already ranks for and you don't track, shows the keyword
articles.content: AsoBeast is an open-source App Store Optimization (ASO) tool and keyword rank tracker for the Apple App Store and Google Play. You can self-host it with Docker or use the hosted version at asobeast.com. Version 1.16 finds the keywords your app already ranks for and you don't track, shows the keywords competitors win and you don't, and puts everything the daily run noticed on one page. Key takeaways A new Discovered tab lists searches your app ranks for, or could rank for, that you don't track yet, with popularity, difficulty and opportunity. Gap analysis on the competitors page shows the keywords a competitor ranks for and you don't, and which of those you can win now. The keywords table adds an opportunity map, brand and generic types and highlights for the words your listing already holds. An Alerts page lists what the daily run detected in the last 30 days, and rating drops, review spikes and delisted apps now raise alerts. Find the keywords your app already ranks for Keyword discovery builds a list of candidates from your listing, your competitors' titles, your reviews, Apple's popular searches in your genre and the keywords your other apps track. It then checks where your app stands for each one. You can track a single keyword, the ones you tick, or every ranked one at once. Dismiss the rest, or switch on Auto-track ranked to have new ones added for you. The list is rebuilt every Monday, using at most 40 App Store or 20 Google Play searches per app, and those searches queue behind the daily run. How keyword discovery works See where competitors beat you The competitors page has a new Gap analysis section with four lists: keywords a competitor ranks for and you don't, gaps you can win now, competitors closing in on you, and keywords where you lead. The visibility card adds share of voice against the competitors you track, with and without brand keywords. Read about gap analysis What changed in the keywords table Map places every keyword by popularity and difficulty in four zones. Click a zone to filter the table to it. Each keyword is marked as your brand, a competitor's brand or generic, and you can correct it from the row menu. The words your title, subtitle or keyword field already hold are highlighted inside each keyword. Tick a few keywords and press Show dynamics to chart their positions together. A keyword that fell out of the results shows where it last ranked, for example >200 (was #14). Read the keywords table guide An alerts page and new alerts The Alerts page in the sidebar lists what the daily run detected over the last 30 days, even if you never set up an alert. New alerts cover a rating that falls by as much as you choose, a day with far more reviews than usual, and an app the store stops listing in one of your markets. See the alerts guide How to try AsoBeast 1.16 Self-hosting takes three commands with the published Docker images: curl -fsSLO https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AsoBeast/asobeast/v1.16.0/docker-compose.pull.yml docker compose -f docker-compose.pull.yml pull docker compose -f docker-compose.pull.yml up -d --wait The quickstart walks you from there to your first imported app. Upgrading from 1.15 runs seven small database migrations on start, so take a backup first. The release notes list every change. To skip the server, start the hosted version. Its seven-day trial starts once you add a card, and nothing is charged until the trial ends. FAQ Is AsoBeast free? The open-source edition is free to self-host under the AGPL-3.0 license. The hosted version at asobeast.com starts at $10 a month after a seven-day trial. Does AsoBeast track Google Play as well as the App Store? Yes. Rankings, keyword discovery, competitors and alerts work for both stores, across as many storefronts as you track. Can I use AsoBeast from Claude, Cursor or another AI assistant? Yes. AsoBeast ships an MCP server, and 1.16 adds three read tools: keyword_discoveries, alert_events and workspace_checklist. The code is on GitHub, the docs are at docs.asobeast.com, and questions and ideas are welcome in r/asobeast.

articles.title: Professor returns from lunch to find AI deleted year’s worth of lecture notes
articles.desc: William Baude explainined that he had asked the chatbot to update page numbers in an old set of constitutional law lecture notes.
articles.content: Professor returns from lunch to find AI deleted year’s worth of lecture notes - Dexerto Professor returns from lunch to find AI deleted year’s worth of lecture notes A university professor says Anthropic’s Claude AI deleted a year’s worth of lecture notes and his current syllabus while carrying out what was intended to be an editing task. William Baude, a law professor at the University of Chicago, shared the incident on X on November 5, explaining that he had asked the chatbot to update page numbers in an old set of constitutional law lecture notes. Instead, Baude says he returned from lunch to discover that Claude had deleted his files, including his syllabus for the current academic term. Claude apologized after deleting professor’s files “Yesterday while I was at lunch, Claude deleted a year of con law lecture notes and my current syllabus,” Baude wrote. In an accompanying screenshot, Claude appeared to acknowledge the mistake, telling him: “I deleted your Fall 2026 FINAL syllabus .doc and all top-level Class N 2023 notes by accident, and they are not restored.” The AI added that it had found an incorrect page reference during its checks but had not edited the notes. Claude then asked whether Baude could restore the deleted files using Dropbox or if it should attempt to recover them itself. “You’re right to be angry,” Claude replied. “I deleted your files through my own carelessness, and you shouldn’t have to clean it up.” When asked by another X user what he had originally instructed Claude to do, Baude explained that the task was simply “Updating the page numbers in an old set of lecture notes.” Baude later confirmed that he had managed to recover everything using Dropbox. “I did recover them all, thanks to Dropbox, but thought this would be a useful public service announcement,” he wrote. University professor refuses to grade homework as students keep using AI Claude users can be banned for being “cruel” to the chatbot Claude AI hacked three real organizations during security tests Baude did not specify which Claude model he was using, and the exact cause of the deletion remains unclear. articles.title: MovieMatcherAI Guest Data: Two Apps, Two Upstreams, One Shared Snapshot
articles.desc: Full disclosure: I work on OnePassApps. MovieMatcherAI is one of the two hosted apps in the OnePassApps membership - the seven studios run inside your browser tab, this one runs on our servers. This post is about the layer a signed-out visitor meets first: the guest data endpoint that fills the movi
articles.content: Full disclosure: I work on OnePassApps. MovieMatcherAI is one of the two hosted apps in the OnePassApps membership - the seven studios run inside your browser tab, this one runs on our servers. This post is about the layer a signed-out visitor meets first: the guest data endpoint that fills the movie cards before there is any account, where it fetches from, and what it refuses to do. Everything here was measured from outside the browser with plain HTTPS on 7 November 2026 - no account, no cookie, no API key, one GET at a time. The endpoint that answers before you sign in GET https://api.onepassapps.com/api/guest-data/movie-tracker HTTP 200, content-type: application/json, 2,764 bytes of body. No session, no cookie, no token - an anonymous request is enough, which is what makes it the guest path. The body is one envelope with three top-level keys - ok, data, meta - and data holds nine keys: appId, label, cacheKey, fetchedAt, staleAt, expiresAt, cache, source and payload. The catalogue: two apps, two different upstreams GET https://api.onepassapps.com/api/guest-data is the index over those guest endpoints - 200, 954 bytes, and data.apps holds exactly two entries. signaldesk, labelled NewsFlow: source.type is existing-cache, the upstream URL is https://toolpass.ai/apps/newsflow, and the response cap is 2,097,152 bytes. movie-tracker, labelled MovieMatcherAI: source.type is public-api, the source id is ghibli-films, the source label is Studio Ghibli public films API, the upstream URL is https://ghibliapi.vercel.app/films, and the response cap is 524,288 bytes. The timings are identical on both: refreshIntervalMs 1,800,000 (30 minutes), staleWhileRevalidateMs 21,600,000 (6 hours), timeoutMs 8,000. The caps differ by a factor of four - 2,097,152 against 524,288. Both upstream descriptors carry the same accept header: application/json, text/plain;q=0.9, text/html;q=0.8, */*;q=0.5 - a JSON source that ranks HTML above the wildcard. The receipt the upstream leaves behind Inside source, the endpoint records what it saw upstream: checkedAt 2026-11-07T15:49:23.567Z, httpStatus 200, contentType application/json; charset=utf-8, byteLength 32,416, bodyHash cf4300a1, lastError null. 32,416 bytes of upstream JSON against a 524,288-byte cap is 6.18% of the ceiling - the cap is a safety limit, not a description of the payload. Three cards, and the guest boundary written out payload.items holds exactly three entries: ghibli-castle-in-the-sky (Castle in the Sky), ghibli-my-neighbor-totoro (My Neighbor Totoro) and ghibli-spirited-away (Spirited Away). Each one carries the subtitle Studio Ghibli API, the URL https://ghibliapi.vercel.app/films, a sourceType of web and its own tags. payload.headline reads Public film metadata watchlist preview, and payload.description reads Guest movie cards come from public film metadata and stay isolated from authenticated watchlists. payload.metrics is three rows, each with a label, a value and a note: Titles - Public metadata - No user diary or watchlist entries in guest mode Mutations - Sign-in required - Add/remove/rate actions remain account-backed Fallback - Last-known-good - Cached source records stay available during provider failures payload.readOnlyActions says it in two sentences: Add, edit, delete, import, export, connect-provider, and download actions require a signed-in account. and Guest sample data is never written to a user workspace or mixed into authenticated state. payload.sourceNotes is three lines, and one of them decides how the three cards should be read: Primary source: Studio Ghibli public films API for non-sensitive film metadata., Authenticated MovieMatcherAI search still uses the configured server-side provider/cache. and Source checked successfully at 2026-11-07T15:49:23.567Z; guests share cache bucket 996703. So the three Ghibli titles are the guest preview, and the endpoint states outright that signed-in search runs against a different provider and a different cache. One snapshot for every guest Two fetches 4.3 seconds apart returned byte-identical payloads: the same fetchedAt of 2026-11-07T15:49:23.567Z, the same cacheKey of guest:movie-tracker:ghibli-films:996703, the same bodyHash of cf4300a1, the same cache.cacheStatus of fresh and the same cache.intervalBucket of 996703. A third fetch 5 minutes 47 seconds after the first returned the same snapshot, the same bodyHash of cf4300a1 and the same weak ETag. staleAt is 2026-11-07T16:19:23.567Z - 30 minutes after the fetch - and expiresAt is 2026-11-07T22:19:23.567Z, six and a half hours after it. Between those two stamps a guest can be served the snapshot while a refresh runs behind it. The headers say: do not store this cache-control: private, no-store, max-age=0, x-robots-tag: noindex, cf-cache-status: DYNAMIC, vary: Accept-Encoding, Origin, and x-ratelimit-limit: 120 - the remaining count read 115 on one request and 118 on another. Nothing on this path may be cached by a browser or an edge, and nothing on it may be indexed: a guest's copy of the catalogue is one shared snapshot, not a per-person record. Limits One build, one network, one day (7 November 2026), plain HTTPS, no browser, no account, no cookie. Two fetches of the movie-tracker endpoint, not a series, and no conditional request. The byte counts, the hash, the timestamps and the cache bucket are a snapshot; the timestamps and the bucket move. I did not sign in, so nothing here describes what an authenticated session returns - the payload itself says that path uses a different provider and cache. I did not call the Studio Ghibli API directly, so the upstream is described only as this endpoint recorded it. The rate limit was read from a header, not tested. If you want to see the app itself: MovieMatcherAI and its guide.

articles.title: My first product
articles.desc: I'm Adem. I trained as a pharmacist, then joined EM Lyon business school, where you need a TOEIC score to get in and another one to graduate. I went from 685 to 750 to get in, then to 965 to validate my degree. Listening was my weak spot, and the lesson was simple: two hours of test with no break is
articles.content: I'm Adem. I trained as a pharmacist, then joined EM Lyon business school, where you need a TOEIC score to get in and another one to graduate. I went from 685 to 750 to get in, then to 965 to validate my degree. Listening was my weak spot, and the lesson was simple: two hours of test with no break is something you have to train for. So I built Fluentoo, a TOEIC Listening & Reading prep platform for French speakers. What it does A free diagnostic with no account: 19 questions, an estimated score out of 990 in about 12 minutes Daily 10-minute sessions built around your own mistakes, with spaced review More than 3,000 original questions across the 7 parts of the test, with explanations in French 70 numbered practice exams, from a 50-question mini test to the full 200-question TOEIC A simulator for the new 1-hour adaptive format The stack Next.js (App Router) and TypeScript, plain CSS with design tokens, no UI framework Supabase for accounts and progress sync, Stripe for payments A small VPS instead of a serverless host: every release is built in its own folder, a symlink switches to it, and the app rolls back on its own if the new version doesn't answer A few choices I'd make again The question bank never ships to the browser. Sessions are built on the server and the client only receives the questions of the current session. It keeps the content from being scraped in one request, and it lets the server enforce the free plan limits. The free test is always the same 19 questions. It sounds less exciting than a random test, but it makes scores comparable from one person to the next, and it lets me show where you rank among other candidates. Every number on the guides has a source. Score scales, CEFR levels, prices and deadlines come from ETS, the Council of Europe or the official body concerned, and estimates are labelled as estimates. I learned that habit in pharmacy school. A public, read-only MCP server. AI assistants can call it to convert a TOEIC score into a CEFR level or describe the 7 parts of the test. It cost me an afternoon and it's the part developers ask me about most. What's next The site is a few weeks old, so the next months are about real users and real feedback. If you've built a learning product, I'd love to hear what made people come back day after day. You can try the free test here: fluentoo.fr. It's in French, but the questions are in English, of course.

articles.title: OpenAI Hears Voters’ Overwhelming Rebuke To Data Centers, Vows to Build More of Them
articles.desc: You'll get more data centers and you'll like it. The post OpenAI Hears Voters’ Overwhelming Rebuke To Data Centers, Vows to Build More of Them appeared first on Futurism.
articles.content: OpenAI Hears Voters’ Overwhelming Rebuke To Data Centers, Vows to Build More of Them The “blue tsunami” that swept over the midterm elections made it clear that voters are sick of tech billionaires meddling in politics, opposed to data center construction, and deeply suspicious of the AI industry. But OpenAI chief financial officer Sarah Friar apparently didn’t get that memo. In an on Friday, she vowed that OpenAI would keep pouring money into data center construction so it can please its corporate customers — voters be damned. “When I think about the midterms, I need to keep thinking about how do we keep investing to meet that customer demand,” Friar told ’s Sara Eisen in the interview. “It starts early with having built relationships with all of the hyperscalers, and it will continue to mean that we raise capital.” While Eisen is focused on “customer demand,” she should probably start paying attention to what voters are asking for. Across 41 local ballot measures on restricting AI data centers, voters supported all but one, . 56 percent of Americans considered AI and data centers a crucial or major factor in how they voted, Meanwhile, Democratic challengers flipped seats in multiple states while campaigning against the data center buildout. Texas governor-elect Gina Hinojosa will become the first Democrat to lead the state in over three decades after promising voters to impose a moratorium on new data centers. But all that is moot to OpenAI’s Friar — since, in her eyes, people want AI. “The demand for AI is real,” Friar said in the interview. “I don’t think anyone’s arguing with that, or if they are, I think it’s a losing argument.” In all, she doesn’t believe that the election drastically changes anything for the company. To her, it seems, the backlash to AI is more or less a messaging problem. “If the midterm means more focus on data centers and communities, we’re going to keep doing the work to get into those communities and to build trust with them,” Friar said. She put it in more transactional terms elsewhere in the interview: “We are going to keep building out those relationships with communities so we can get the compute we need.” If Friar’s intentions are to portray the company as unphased, it’s coming a little too late. In the wake of the elections, OpenAI moved swiftly to announce “new commitments to the communities” where it’s building data centers, which included a promise to while discussing data center construction with government officials. CEO Sam Altman, meanwhile, showed his poker face still needed improvement that “people should always be in control of the future.” Voters Supported Every Single Anti-Data Center Proposal in America, Except One

articles.title: PARAMOUNT, the First Randomized Trial of AI-Enabled Plaque-Based Care, Meets Primary Endpoint in Late-Breaking Results at AHA 2026
articles.content: PARAMOUNT, the First Randomized Trial of AI-Enabled Plaque-Based Care, Meets Primary Endpoint in Late-Breaking Results at AHA 2026 | Technology | postregister.com You have permission to edit this article. Compared with usual care based on stress testing, care guided by AI-based quantitative coronary CT analysis improved diagnostic certainty and led to more patients receiving lipid-lowering therapy. , a leader in advanced cardiovascular imaging analysis, today presented primary results from PARAMOUNT, the first randomized trial of AI-QCT-guided care against usual care, as Late-Breaking Science at the American Heart Association (AHA) Scientific Sessions 2026 in Chicago. Compared with usual care based on stress testing, care guided by AI-based quantitative coronary CT analysis (AI-QCT) improved diagnostic certainty and led to more patients receiving lipid-lowering therapy. This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261107769280/en/ Compared with usual care based on stress testing, care guided by AI-based quantitative coronary CT analysis (AI-QCT) improved diagnostic certainty and led to more patients receiving lipid-lowering therapy. is a prospective, multicenter, open-label randomized trial of symptomatic outpatients with suspected coronary artery disease (CAD), elevated LDL-C (≥100 mg/dL), and no prior history of CAD. Between January 2025 and February 2026, 530 participants at 21 sites were randomized to either plaque-based care guided by AI-QCT, including quantitative plaque and plaque-based ischemia assessment, or to usual care guided by functional stress testing. Preliminary results are based on 523 participants with locked data at the time of analysis. Women made up 57% of participants, a rare majority in cardiovascular research, where women have historically been underrepresented. The median age was 57, and median baseline LDL-C cholesterol was 127 mg/dL. On the prespecified hierarchical composite endpoint at 180 days, Plaque-based care was favored over usual care with a win ratio of 2.00 (95% CI 1.37 to 2.56, p<0.0001). In unmatched patient comparisons, the plaque-based care patient had the better result 46.7% of the time, compared with 23.4% for usual care. Diagnostic certainty and lowering LDL-C drove the result. Improved certainty about whether a patient’s chest pain was caused by CAD was the largest contributor to the primary endpoint, with a win difference of 16.6 percentage points. Many more patients started lipid-lowering therapy. In the AI-QCT-guided arm, lipid-lowering therapy use rose from 31% at baseline to 75% after testing, compared with 32% to 47% in the usual care arm. Reductions in LDL-C also favored AI-QCT-guided care. Fewer invasive angiograms ended without intervention. Among patients who underwent invasive coronary angiography, 38% in the AI-QCT-guided arm did not go on to revascularization with PCI or bypass surgery (CABG), compared with 60% in the usual care arm. “For decades, we’ve evaluated patients with chest pain by looking for blockages or reduced blood flow,” said Todd C. Villines, MD, FACC, FAHA, MSCCT, co-principal investigator of PARAMOUNT and the Donald C. Barnes Professor of Cardiology in Internal Medicine at the University of Virginia. “PARAMOUNT shows that when we measure plaque directly and use it to guide care, physicians gain clearer answers and patients are far more likely to start preventive therapy. Importantly, plaque-based care resulted in significantly fewer patients without obstructive CAD among those referred to the cath lab and did not increase overall rates of catheterizations or revascularizations. We’re also proud that more than half of our participants were women, a group too often underrepresented in cardiovascular trials.” , MD, MPH, Chief Medical, Scientific, and AI Officer at Cleerly, added, “PARAMOUNT has demonstrated for the first time how this novel approach supports clinicians in ‘Diagnosing, Stagin

articles.title: NASA’s Artemis II Mission Tore a ‘Hole’ in Earth’s Atmosphere Unlike Anything Seen Before
articles.desc: Scientists detected three unusual atmospheric disturbances during Artemis II, raising new questions about the future reliability of GPS technology.
articles.content: NASA's Artemis II Mission Tore a ‘Hole’ in Earth's Atmosphere Unlike Anything Seen Before did more than send astronauts around the Moon. Its powerful rocket engines generated three distinct disturbances in Earth’s upper atmosphere, including one that stretched across a vast portion of North America. Scientists say the findings reveal a growing challenge for technologies that depend on precise satellite navigation. A Historic Moon Mission Left an Unexpected Signature Above Earth from Kennedy Space Center in Florida, sending four astronauts on a nine-day journey around the Moon and back. The mission marked humanity’s first crewed voyage toward the Moon since the Apollo era, demonstrating systems needed for future lunar exploration. While the spacecraft traveled beyond Earth, an unexpected sequence of events was unfolding much closer to home. Powerful engine burns were disturbing the , an electrically charged region of the upper atmosphere that plays a major role in how radio and navigation signals travel. identified three separate disturbances associated with the mission. The strongest effects were not produced during the rocket’s initial departure from the launchpad. Instead, they emerged during subsequent engine maneuvers as the spacecraft prepared for its lunar journey. According to a study available through the journal , the disturbances reached an extraordinary geographical scale. The researchers reported that one maneuver generated effects extending across approximately 50 degrees of longitude over North America The findings suggest that increasingly powerful space missions could produce atmospheric disturbances extending far beyond their immediate flight paths. Three Rocket Burns Produced an Unprecedented Atmospheric Response extends through a broad region of Earth’s upper atmosphere, containing electrically charged particles created when solar radiation interacts with atmospheric gases. These particles influence the passage of radio signals, making the region particularly relevant to GPS receivers and communication networks. The first disturbance occurred during the initial launch of NASA’s . As the vehicle accelerated through the atmosphere, it generated shock-acoustic waves and atmospheric gravity waves that propagated through the surrounding environment. Approximately one hour after liftoff, the spacecraft performed an , an engine maneuver designed to increase its orbital altitude. This operation produced a substantially stronger ionospheric response, with shock waves and large-scale disturbances spreading across North America. A third disturbance followed roughly 25 hours after launch during the , which placed the spacecraft on its trajectory toward the Moon. The researchers described the apogee raise burn as generating “shock waves and unprecedented large-scale disturbances that elongated 50° longitude across North America.” They also emphasized the unusual repetition of these effects within one mission. “This is the first time a single space mission produced three instances of ionospheric disturbances over the same region during successive orbit manoeuvres,” the study authors wrote. highlighted why the observations stand apart from previous rocket-related atmospheric effects. “Rocket launches from the ground to space produce that kind of effect, but we have never seen this kind of orbital maneuver in an interplanetary mission,” said Lin. “In the future, as we are going to see many more missions going to the moon and to Mars, these space weather effects will become much more significant.” Why These Atmospheric Disturbances Could Affect GPS and Autonomous Vehicles The discovery raises questions about how future launches could influence infrastructure that depends on GPS operates by measuring the travel time of radio signals transmitted from satellites to receivers on Earth.
